solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Sir ideal to become PM

indicators.note: the letters of the two words turn into something else, so they are to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A knight held up as a model is destined to lead the government.
explanation.definitionFit: Benjamin Disraeli served twice as British Prime Minister in the nineteenth century, an example of the abbreviation PM.

clue.text: Character outside gym complained

indicators.note: the first piece sits on the outside of the second, wrapping round it

parts.note: a character, an eccentric person, is a card
gym as a school subject is PE, physical education

explanation.surface: An eccentric moaned about the gymnasium.
explanation.definitionFit: To carp is to find fault or grumble, so the past tense is a synonym for complained.

clue.text: Finishing second? Excellent!

parts.note: topping is dated British slang for excellent

explanation.surface: Someone crossing the line in second place celebrates the result.
explanation.walkthrough: TOPPING is old-fashioned British slang meaning first-rate.
explanation.definitionFit: Stopping and finishing are synonyms, both meaning bringing to an end.

clue.text: What songs are turned up for the Animals

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means the letters are read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: songs are sung, so the phrase gives that participle

explanation.surface: Seems to ask which songs were played loud for the 1960s band The Animals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Animals' looks like the rock band; it is simply a plural noun for beasts.
explanation.definitionFit: Gnus are wildebeest, a kind of African antelope, so they are examples of animals.

clue.text: What should be easy task — is one 'hampered'?

definitions.meaning: an easy job is called this informally, as in 'it was no ...'
an outdoor meal is often packed in a hamper, so playfully it is hampered

explanation.surface: Wonders whether an easy job is being obstructed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hampered' looks like hindered; it means packed in a wicker basket.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal idiom calls an easy undertaking this, and an outdoor meal is traditionally carried in a hamper.

clue.text: Magritte's inner strength of character

indicators.note: the inner letters of the painter's name are the source of the word

explanation.surface: Praises the Belgian surrealist painter Magritte for his inner fortitude.
explanation.definitionFit: Grit is courage and resolve, a synonym for strength of character.

clue.text: Travel document is needed in Virginia

indicators.note: the word is goes inside the state abbreviation

parts.note: VA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Virginia

explanation.surface: A passport stamp or permit is required for entry to Virginia.
explanation.definitionFit: A visa is an endorsement allowing entry to a country, an example of a travel document.

clue.text: Great sin ruined African city

indicators.note: something ruined is wrecked, so the letters are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: A grave moral failing brought a city in Africa to ruin.
explanation.definitionFit: Tangiers is a port city in northern Morocco, an example of an African city.

clue.text: Support for cheeky youngster

parts.note: pro means in favour of, as in pros and cons
a pup is an impudent young man, an old-fashioned usage

explanation.surface: Offering backing to an impudent youth.
explanation.definitionFit: To prop up is a phrasal verb meaning to hold up or sustain, a synonym for support.

clue.text: Nationalist coming within view in governing body

indicators.note: the abbreviation goes inside the word for view

parts.note: to view is to see

explanation.surface: A nationalist politician becomes visible in the legislature.
explanation.definitionFit: A senate is a legislative assembly, such as the upper house of a parliament, an example of a governing body.

clue.text: Chaps beginning to doubt put right

parts.note: chaps are men

indicators.note: the beginning of the next word supplies its first letter

explanation.surface: Some men began to have doubts and corrected things.
explanation.definitionFit: To mend is to repair or fix, a synonym for put right.

clue.text: Nice and sure? Quite otherwise!

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are to be put quite otherwise, in a different order

explanation.surface: Asks if someone is pleasant and confident, then retorts that they are the very opposite.
explanation.walkthrough: Otherwise than sure is unsure, so the whole clue also defines the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Being far from sure is the meaning of lacking confidence or certainty.

clue.text: Senior common room, very small, in which university's held examination

indicators.note: the senior common room and the small word together form a container for the next piece
the letter for university is held inside, in the middle of the pair

parts.note: SCR is the abbreviation for senior common room, the staff lounge of a British college
very small means tiny
U is the abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: A tiny staff lounge at a university is where an exam takes place.
explanation.walkthrough: A senior common room is the room for academic staff at a British university or college.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrutiny is close inspection, a synonym for examination.

clue.text: Revolutionary monarch, old person effecting change

indicators.note: something revolving turns round, so the queen's abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen
former means old or previous

explanation.surface: A king who once rebelled is a figure for change.
explanation.definitionFit: A reformer campaigns for improvement in institutions, a person bringing about change.

clue.text: Servant runs briefly to catch bad robber

indicators.note: the servant word catches the next piece, holding it inside

parts.note: a page is a boy servant
ill means bad, as in ill will
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A servant hurries off to apprehend a criminal thief.
explanation.definitionFit: A pillager plunders and loots, a kind of robber.

clue.text: A large crumbling encampment

indicators.note: something crumbling falls apart, so these letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A big structure is falling to pieces at the camp.
explanation.definitionFit: A laager is a defensive camp ringed by wagons, a South African term for an encampment.

clue.text: Polish expert

definitions.meaning: to shine or rub to a gloss
an enthusiast who knows a lot, as in a film fan

explanation.definitionFit: To buff is to polish to a shine, and a buff is an enthusiast with expert knowledge.

clue.text: Fade, being left buried in sand?

indicators.note: the abbreviation for left goes inside the word for sand

parts.note: a beach is a stretch of sand

explanation.surface: Asks whether something fades when it is abandoned under the sand.
explanation.definitionFit: To bleach is to lose colour, as fabric does in sunlight, a synonym for fade.

clue.text: Danger from extreme characters in firm

indicators.note: the extreme letters go inside the word for firm

parts.note: firm means hard
A and Z are the extreme letters of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A company faces risk from people at the margins.
explanation.definitionFit: A hazard is a risk or peril, a synonym for danger.

clue.text: A married seaman in a holy book

parts.note: OS stands for ordinary seaman

explanation.surface: A wedded sailor appears in scripture.
explanation.definitionFit: Amos is one of the minor prophets and a book of the Old Testament, an example of a holy book.

clue.text: Get rid of awful noise outside front of office

indicators.note: the noise word goes outside the initial letter

parts.note: a din is a loud unpleasant noise

indicators.note: the front of the word office is its first letter

explanation.surface: A command to stop a racket happening outside the office entrance.
explanation.definitionFit: To do in is a slang idiom meaning to kill, so to get rid of someone.

clue.text: Politician harbouring explosive idea

indicators.note: the politician harbours, holding inside, the abbreviation for explosive

parts.note: a Tory is a British Conservative politician
HE is high explosive

explanation.surface: A politician is sheltering a dangerous notion.
explanation.definitionFit: A theory is a proposed explanation or notion, a synonym for idea.

clue.text: Bishop in a home surprisingly unconventional

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

indicators.note: the letters behave in an unexpected way, ending up rearranged

explanation.surface: A cleric living at home is, astonishingly, a free spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a home' looks like the place the bishop is; those three words are the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A bohemian lives free of social conventions, artistic and unorthodox, so the word means unconventional.

clue.text: Head dismissing one member of kitchen team

indicators.note: dismissing sends away the numeral for one

parts.note: a chief is a head or leader
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A boss sacks one of the restaurant staff.
explanation.definitionFit: A chef is a cook, one of those working in a restaurant kitchen.
